summary: Utah: WillhiteWeb lists Meadow Creek Peak among sites it has not visited and guesses the name refers to a creek. No lookout history was found.

evidence.supports: the list places Meadow Creek Peak under sites the author has not visited
author guesses the name refers to a creek draining the Pahvant Range (this entry has no county line, so the match to this name is inferred from its position in the list)
evidence.quote: If I had to guess, the location is referencing the Meadow Creek that drains the highest peaks of the Pahvant Range.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Meadow Creek Peak in Box Elder County at these coordinates

notes_for_editor: Story withheld. The only sourced text is an unvisited-site listing and a guess about the name. That cannot reach the 120-word floor without padding, and no source confirms a lookout here. Unresolved conflict: the Forest Fire Lookout Association places the point in Box Elder County, while WillhiteWeb's guess ties the name to the Pahvant Range in Millard County. The GNIS summit table (local data/sources/peaks_gnis.json, retrieved 2026-10-04) names the same coordinates 'Meadow Creek Butte' (UT), not a peak, so the record name may be wrong. Two web searches found no Utah lookout by this name and no county for it. Suggest holding the record out of publication until a source is found. Next step: Utah Division of Forestry, Fire and State Lands or the Utah State Historic Preservation Office.
